title: Dead man's mother charged with conspiring to kill cop, neighbour in police shooting on Queen Frederica Drive
article: The mother of a man who was shot and killed by police in Friday night's wild encounter on Queen Frederica Drive has been charged with conspiring to murder a police officer and a neighbour.

The News has learned through multiple sources that Boketsu Boekwa, 50, who lived in the townhouse complex where the chaotic scene unfolded late Friday (March 20), has been charged with two counts of conspiracy to commit murder, along with one count each of assault with a weapon and uttering threats. She was in court Tuesday and was remanded in custody until her next appearance, a bail hearing scheduled for March 27. There's been a publication ban placed on evidence given in court.

Police allege Boekwa conspired with her son, identified as Marc Ekamba-Boekwa, 22, to kill a police officer and a neighbour. She is further accused of assaulting a female neighbour with a weapon and threatening her.

Ekamba-Boekwa was fatally wounded during the encounter with Peel Police officers, who were called to the scene after a 9-1-1 call alleging someone was making death threats, according to well-placed sources.

The province's Special Investigations Unit (SIU) continues to probe the circumstances that led to the man being fatally shot by police during the volatile encounter at the townhouse complex, near Dixie Road and Dundas Street East.

Two Peel officers were wounded during the clash. Both were stabbed and one was shot, according to police. Both male officers, who've been with the force seven years and five years respectively, have been released from hospital and are recovering at their homes. A 21-year-old woman identified as Humber College student Suzan Zreik, also received a gunshot wound in the incident and is recovering. Zreik was hit by a stray bullet and not directly involved in the shooting incident.
SIU spokesperson Monica Hudon confirmed a female officer and two male officers are the subject of the investigation. There are seven witness officers.

One of the injured officers, a seven-year veteran of the force and former Ontario Hockey League (OHL) player, received a letter of merit from the Ontario government and a police commendation for his efforts in trying to rescue a woman who jumped into the frigid waters of Lake Ontario back in November 2010. He helped bring the woman, and another officer who went in to rescue her, to land. Despite performing CPR, the woman died of her injuries.
On Friday night, he, along with other officers, were called to the scene after a 9-1-1 call to Peel Regional Police alleging a man was making death threats, according to well-placed sources.
Neither Peel police nor the SIU will say what exactly sent police to the scene just after 10:30 p.m., with the provincial watchdog only saying police were called there "for assistance."
However, two sources close to the case have told The News a 9-1-1 call was made alleging a disturbance in which someone was making threats.
The SIU said officers arrived at about 10:40 p.m. After an "interaction" between police and the man, he was shot multiple times. The man was pronounced dead at the scene.
The injured woman was taken to hospital after being hit by a bullet that came through her window. She has since been released from hospital.
Neighbours in the townhouse complex said the dead man, who lived in a townhouse with his mother and a woman believed to be his sister, had been terrorizing them for more than a year.

Brenda Bilow, who has lived in the townhouse complex for 16 years, said she wasn't home when the confrontation between the man and police occurred. However, she was told by others in the complex that the incident reportedly began as a dispute between neighbours.
"It's scary, it's scary," said Bilow. "We knew something like this would happen. Police were called here many times. Neighbours had called police because they were making death threats."
Rachel Firlotte, whose townhouse backs onto the road where the incident took place, said she heard about 10 gunshots sometime after 10:30 p.m.

"I was in my living room watching TV, and I could hear the commotion of an argument - and within three seconds it was screaming, shouting, the gunfire," she said. "I got up to look and saw the guy dead on the ground. I was about to call 9-1-1 but then I noticed the police were already here."
Firlotte alleged the dead man recently threatened to kill another neighbour's family and all the children in the area, amid an ongoing dispute that began months ago but escalated earlier this week.
"He was a very scary person," Firlotte said. "I tried to avoid him at all costs."
Bilow described the family as "very unpredictable people," and she said she lived in fear of the man who was fatally shot.
"I was always afraid of them. He was really scary. His look was very piercing. Something about him was not right," she said.
Anyone who may have information regarding this incident should call police at 905-453-2121 or the SIU's lead investigator at 1-800-787-8529, ext. 1935.
